rationale: Round 0 built and ran correctly, so this round pushes obfuscation strength up on the dimensions that matter for this target: a tiny (388-byte text, 3-function) floating-point-heavy numeric benchmark with no security-critical surface, where the goal is maximizing static/dynamic analysis resistance rather than protecting secrets. BCF gets the highest SecurityGain since opaque predicates defeat both static control-flow recovery and symbolic execution cheaply, and its RuntimeCost/SizeCost weights are raised to accept its overhead given the minuscule code size leaves ample headroom. FLA stays high to destroy the simple loop structure that dominates this benchmark, with CorrectnessRisk held at 0.3 since floating-point-heavy flattened loops previously built and ran fine. SUB is favored because the benchmark is arithmetic-dense (its integer-side substitutions compose with FLA/BCF for layered resistance), while IBR and ICALL add indirect-control-flow indirection at low risk. SPLIT, IGV, and their cost dimensions are kept low: functions this small offer few basic blocks to split and few globals to indirect, so spending selection budget there buys little; their modest nonzero weights let them apply opportunistically where features favor them without displacing the high-gain passes. Overall the table trades size overhead (plentiful headroom in a 388-byte binary) for maximum control-flow and data-transform diversity, while keeping CorrectnessRisk uniformly low to preserve the build/run correctness already demonstrated.
